articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Elche vs Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Elche y al Real Madrid en el Martínez Valero correspondiente a la sexta jornada de LaLiga
articles.summary: Codere te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Elche y al Real Madrid en el Martínez Valero correspondiente a la sexta jornada de LaLiga
articles.body: El Elche recibe al Real Madrid este martes en el Martínez Valero, en el partido correspondiente a la sexta jornada de LaLiga 26/27. El conjunto ilicitano afronta el encuentro en una situación muy delicada. Es penúltimo clasificado con solo un punto de quince posibles y arrastra la peor defensa de LaLiga, con 15 goles encajados en sus cinco primeras jornadas, la última derrota por 2-3 ante la Real Sociedad, en un partido en el que llegó a remontar antes de encajar el tanto decisivo en el descuento. Favorito para el partido entre Elche y Real Madrid Por su parte, el Real Madrid llega a tierras alicantinas en un estado de forma arrollador. El conjunto de Mourinho firmó un nuevo festival de goles en su último compromiso, un 4-1 ante el Rayo Vallecano con doblete de Mbappé y tantos de Carreras y Bellingham, resultado que confirma el pleno de victorias del equipo blanco como local esta temporada: 4-1 a la Real Sociedad, 4-0 al Málaga y ahora 4-1 al Rayo, con 12 goles a favor y solo uno en contra en esos tres partidos en el Bernabéu. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como amplio favorito al Real Madrid. Codere paga la victoria visitante a cuota 1.28, por 5.5 del empate y 7.50 de la victoria del cuadro ilicitano. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. El Elche ha encajado en todos sus partidos disputados esta temporada, mostrando serias carencias defensivas, mientras que el Real Madrid tampoco ha dejado su portería a cero en su última salida, encajando el gol de Camello ante el Rayo. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten es alta. Codere paga a 1.6 el "sí" y a 2.2 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con mucha producción ofensiva. El Real Madrid ha marcado 12 goles en sus tres últimos partidos como visitante o local, mientras que el Elche, pese a sus problemas defensivos, también ha demostrado capacidad para ver puerta en la mayoría de sus salidas. Con estos datos, Codere sitúa la cuota del +3.5 totales a 1.88, por 1.85 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Real Madrid, con su juego de posesión y dominio territorial, suele generar un volumen alto de saques de esquina en sus desplazamientos, especialmente ante rivales que se ven obligados a replegarse por la diferencia de nivel. El Elche, por su parte, ha mostrado en sus últimas salidas serias dificultades para sostener el balón en campo rival, lo que invita a pensar en una notable diferencia de córners a favor del conjunto blanco en este duelo.

articles.title: Hyrox world record holder Joanna Wietrzyk pooped during race, was allowed to continue and win; organisers now apologise and change rules
articles.summary: More sports News: Global indoor fitness race organiser Hyrox has changed its rules after women's world record holder Joanna Wietrzyk soiled herself during a race in Bei.
articles.body: Global indoor fitness race organiser Hyrox has changed its rules after women's world record holder Joanna Wietrzyk soiled herself during a race in Beijing on Saturday but was allowed to continue and win the event.Moritz Fuerste, Hyrox's German co-founder and a former Olympic field hockey champion, apologised for the way the incident was handled and admitted the organisers should have acted during the race."Hyrox made a mistake by not reacting immediately during the race," Fuerste said in a statement on social media."Of course, we started improving event processes, plus making rulebook changes immediately. As of this moment, there are new rules and procedures in place to prevent situations like this from happening again."Earlier on Monday, Hyrox also said it would permanently ban anyone who sent abuse or threats of violence to Wietrzyk after her identity was shared online."There is no place in our community for threats of violence or encouragement to harm an athlete," Hyrox said in a statement."Any person identified as engaging in this behaviour - whether through comments, direct messages or social media - will be permanently banned from all Hyrox events," it added.Hyrox China and Hyrox World said organisers isolated the affected lanes after the race and carried out deep cleaning before competition resumed the next day. They said contaminated equipment was removed and the venue carpet was replaced overnight.“After the incident, the organising committee immediately closed off and isolated the affected area and track, and completed comprehensive disinfection,” Hyrox China organisers said.Hyrox World said the organisation already had bio-contaminant and medical procedures in place, but those rules were not applied clearly during the event.“Protocols designed for elite competition and mass participation became blurred, creating ambiguity in how they were applied and understood.”Wietrzyk, the women's solo Hyrox world record holder, had been invited to compete in Beijing. After the race, she posted and later deleted a selfie from what appeared to be a hospital bed on her Instagram story.“Go hard or go home … a win is a win. In all seriousness, thank you for all the support. I’ll be back soon x.”Hyrox, which was founded in Hamburg in 2017, combines running with functional fitness exercises in a standardised indoor race format. In each race, participants alternate one-kilometre runs with exercises such as sled pushes, burpee jumps, indoor rowing and sandbag lunges.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Sydney Sweeney faces backlash over sports betting ad as female athletes accuse campaign of sexualizing women in sport: 'How do we live in a world where monetizing a woman's body'
articles.summary: More sports News: An advertising campaign starring American actor Sydney Sweeney has drawn sharp criticism from female athletes, who have accused the campaign of sexual.
articles.body: An advertising campaign starring American actor Sydney Sweeney has drawn sharp criticism from female athletes, who have accused the campaign of sexualising women and undermining the way female athletes are represented in sport.The controversy centres on an ad for sports prediction market platform Novig, in which Sweeney appears wearing little or no clothing. Footballs and other sports equipment are strategically positioned to cover parts of her body.The campaign has prompted a wave of criticism on social media, with several female athletes arguing that the imagery reinforces the sexualisation of women rather than highlighting athletic ability, strength and achievement.Ariarne Titmus questions sexualisation of women's sportFour-time Olympic swimming gold medallist Ariarne Titmus was among those to voice her anger over the campaign."I can't describe how infuriated I feel when I watch this," Titmus wrote on Instagram. "How do we live in a world where monetizing a woman's body and sexualizing women's sport is still a thing?"British sprinter Amy Hunt also weighed in following her fourth-place finish in the 200 metres at the Ultimate Championship in Budapest, Hungary, on Sunday.During a post-race interview with the BBC, Hunt directly addressed Sweeney while looking into the camera."Sydney Sweeney, this is what women in sport look like," she said. "Muscles, hard work, sweat, blood, tears."Former gymnast Gracie Kramer hits out at campaignFormer US gymnast Gracie Kramer described the advertisement as infuriating, drawing on her own experiences as a female athlete."I've spent my entire life competing in a sport where female athletes have been oversexualized, reduced to our bodies, and forced to fight to be taken seriously for what we can actually do," she said on Instagram.Kramer also shared images of female athletes training alongside the caption: “What a woman in sports looks like.”Chinese-German rugby player Sofie Fella similarly criticised the campaign, saying female athletes can serve as role models because they are able to “untangle” themselves from society's expectations surrounding beauty and femininity.“And that's why that Sydney Sweeney ad is so disrespectful to every female athlete in the world,” Fella said in an Instagram post.Sydney Sweeney's apparent responseNovig did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment, while a publicist for Sweeney also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Amid the backlash, Sweeney appeared to reference the debate over the weekend by posting a series of covers from ESPN The Magazine's "Body Issue" on social media.The annual special edition featured athletes posing nude or semi-nude and presented the images as a celebration of different body types.Sweeney, a two-time Emmy nominee, has also played a role connected directly to sport. She starred in and produced last year's “Christy,” a biopic about American professional boxer Christy Martin.The latest controversy is not the first time a Sweeney brand campaign has generated significant online debate. Her 2025 American Eagle campaign, which used the homophones “jeans” and “genes,” also sparked widespread discussion.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Leeds United defeat Newcastle 4-1 to go third in Premier League
articles.summary: Goals from in-form forward Calvert-Lewin, Okafor and Bogle boost Leeds’ standing in the league table.
articles.body:
Leeds United put four goals past Newcastle United in a 4-1 drubbing to climb up to third in the Premier League table and inflict a punishing first defeat for Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle.

A Lewis Miley own goal opened the floodgates before Jayden Bogle, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Noah Okafor completed the rout at Elland Road on Monday.

Newcastle had made a positive start under Jaissle despite the upheaval of losing manager Eddie Howe and key players Anthony Gordon, Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali in the off-season.

Despite being owned by the financial might of the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, Newcastle targeted rising stars to fill the void of those that left and were outmuscled by a more experienced Leeds.

“It was clear from the start and I said that many times that we will have up and downs, challenges along the way,” said Jaissle. “We faced that challenge and it’s tough, it’s really tough.”

A bad night for the visitors began inside the first 20 minutes when Nico Gonzalez had to be replaced as a concussion substitute.

That left 18-year-old Sean Steur and Lewis Miley, 20, together at the heart of the Newcastle midfield and the later unfortunately had the final touch after Ao Tanaka’s strike took two deflections before looping into the net.

The visitors failed to regain their composure as just two minutes later Leeds doubled their advantage.

Calvert-Lewin rose highest to meet James Justin’s cross but his header flicked off Bogle as it found the bottom corner and the right-back was given the goal.

The Leeds’ number nine did not have to wait long to make sure he did score for the fifth consecutive league game at Elland Road.

Calvert-Lewin bulldozed his way past Sven Botman before sliding the ball under Lukas Hornicek in the Newcastle goal.

Anton Stach should have added a fourth early in the second period when he pounced on a slack Hornicek pass out from the pack but dinked the ball just wide.

Okafor did make it 4-0 before the hour mark when he volleyed in from the edge of the box after Newcastle failed to clear a long throw.

“Perfect start right now with eight points, terrific performance,” said Leeds boss Daniel Farke. “Energy, quality and good structure in and without possession.”

Bazoumana Toure netted a consolation in stoppage time to reduce Newcastle’s arrears, but the damage was long since done.

Victory takes Farke’s men behind only defending champions Arsenal and Manchester City.

Newcastle remain on five points but slip down to 12th due to their negative goal difference.

articles.title: El Inter Miami ficha al ex Atleti y Real Madrid Íñigo Aznar como director de ingresos
articles.standfirst: El ejecutivo trabajará junto al también español Xavier Asensi, presidente de operaciones de negocio de la franquicia de la MLS de los hermanos Mas, David Beckham y Leo Messi
articles.summary: El ejecutivo trabajará junto al también español Xavier Asensi, presidente de operaciones de negocio de la franquicia de la MLS de los hermanos Mas, David Beckham y Leo Messi
articles.body: El Inter Miami prosigue con su apuesta por el fútbol español tanto dentro como fuera del césped. La franquicia, vigente campeona de la MLS, ha fichado a Íñigo Aznar como nuevo director de ingresos. El ejecutivo cuenta con 25 años de experiencia en la industria del deporte. Aznar ha ocupado cargos de relevancia en el área comercial del Real Madrid, Atlético de Madrid, Volvo Ocean Race y Legends. En el último año ha estado al frente de la expansión internacional de la Rafa Nadal Academy. En el Inter Miami, el ejecutivo español supervisará las áreas de ingresos y marketing, incluyendo partnerships, ticketing, retail y licencias, food and beverage, además de la nueva plataforma comercial de la compañía, Heron Sports & Entertainment. En Heron trabajará para “atraer grandes eventos, experiencias de entretenimiento, conferencias y reuniones corporativas a las instalaciones de Inter Miami”, destacando el Nu Stadium, el nuevo estadio de la franquicia de Florida que lidera en el campo Leo Messi. Además, el club cuenta con el Florida Blue Training Center, su ciudad deportiva, y el Inter Miami CF Stadium. En su nuevo proyecto, Aznar reportará directamente a Xavier Asensi, presidente de operaciones de negocio del Inter Miami. “La posición de director de ingresos responde a la estrategia que pusimos en marcha hace unos años y, con todo lo que hemos construido en Miami, tiene todo el sentido”, ha destacado el también español Asensi, que llegó al equipo en 2021 procedente del FC Barcelona. “Íñigo cuenta con una trayectoria probada en la creación y el desarrollo de negocio, y su experiencia, liderazgo y visión global le convierten en una excelente incorporación para nuestra organización”, ha agregado. “Incorporarme a Inter Miami supone un gran paso para mí, tanto a nivel profesional como personal”, ha afirmado Aznar sobre su llegada. “Estoy muy ilusionado por trabajar con Xavier y todo el equipo, y aportar mi experiencia global en deporte y entretenimiento para ayudar a llevar a Inter Miami y Heron Sports & Entertainment al siguiente nivel”, ha apuntado el ejecutivo.

articles.title: El Rayo - Espanyol no se mueve de Butarque
articles.standfirst: El club franjirrojo apuró conversaciones con LaLiga y Delegación de Gobierno tras el alzamiento de las medidas cautelares, pero no hay tiempo material para cambiar el dispositivo de seguridad
articles.summary: El club franjirrojo apuró conversaciones con LaLiga y Delegación de Gobierno tras el alzamiento de las medidas cautelares, pero no hay tiempo material para cambiar el dispositivo de seguridad
articles.body: El Rayo-Espanyol se jugará finalmente en Butarque. El club franjirrojo mantuvo conversaciones hasta última hora de la noche con LaLiga y Delegación de Gobierno para estudiar si era viable trasladar el partido a Vallecas, después del alzamiento de las medidas cautelares sobre el estadio, pero la opción ha quedado descartada. El principal obstáculo ha sido la falta de tiempo. El encuentro está declarado de alto riesgo y no existe margen material para modificar todo el dispositivo de seguridad con tan pocas horas de antelación. La organización del partido ya estaba configurada para Butarque y cambiar el escenario a última hora resultaba prácticamente inviable. A ese condicionante se suma el césped de Vallecas. El Rayo está llevando a cabo el cambio del terreno de juego, una actuación que también dificultaba recuperar el estadio de forma inmediata para el duelo ante el Espanyol. El alzamiento de las medidas cautelares abre la puerta al regreso, pero no permite acelerar todos los procesos necesarios para jugar allí de un día para otro. Ante ese escenario, y sin tiempo suficiente para garantizar el traslado del partido a Vallecas, el club franjirrojo llegó a solicitar el aplazamiento del encuentro. La respuesta de LaLiga fue negativa. El partido se mantiene en la fecha prevista y se disputará en Butarque, donde el Rayo volverá a ejercer como local por última vez antes de regresar a su campo. Por lo tanto, la vuelta a Vallecas se producirá el próximo 10 de octubre ante el Athletic. Ese será el primer partido en casa tras semanas marcadas por auditorías, medidas cautelares, traslados y gestiones administrativas. Hasta entonces, Butarque cerrará este paréntesis como refugio provisional del equipo de Beñat San José. En lo deportivo, el Rayo llega al choque después de la derrota en el Bernabéu, pero con el objetivo de mantener su buena dinámica como local en Butarque. Allí, ejerciendo como anfitrión, ha sumado dos victorias, una de ellas contra el Atlético de Madrid el curso pasado, y un empate, una racha que ha permitido amortiguar el impacto de jugar lejos de Vallecas. El Espanyol, por su parte, aterriza tras ganar en Pamplona y con Roberto Fernández como uno de sus grandes argumentos ofensivos. El delantero llega enrachado en cuanto a efectividad y suma cinco goles en lo que va de Liga, solo uno menos que Camello. Un duelo con condicionantes fuera del campo, pero también con un foco claro sobre el césped: el Rayo quiere despedirse de Butarque invicto antes de volver a casa.

articles.summary: El triunfo ante el Villarreal, según Tonybet, asienta a los de Pellegrini como los máximos favoritos para finalizar en el Top-4 de LaLiga
articles.body: La pelea por la cuarta plaza de LaLiga promete ser feroz una temporada más. El Betis, sin embargo, ha conseguido asentarse como el principal favorito para acompañar a Barcelona, Real Madrid y Atlético en el Top-4. El conjunto verdiblanco está protagonizando un inicio de campaña sobresaliente y la victoria ante el Villarreal en La Cerámica, en un duelo directo por la Champions, ha reforzado todavía más sus aspiraciones. La semana para el Betis ha sido impecable: ganaron al Real Madrid, se estrenaron en Champions con una remontada ante el Lille a domicilio y la ha cerrado imponiéndose al Villarreal. Los de Pellegrini ocupan actualmente la tercera posición de la tabla con 12 puntos de 15 posibles, los mismos que el propio Real Madrid. Sólo en la temporada 2011-12, con Pepe Mel en el banquillo, el conjunto verdiblanco consiguió un mejor arranque, con 13 puntos. Las apuestas deportivas también han reaccionado a este espectacular momento de forma. Tonybet ya sitúa al Betis como el máximo favorito para terminar cuarto, con una cuota de 2.20. Por detrás aparecen el Athletic (3.0) y el Villarreal (5.99). La distancia con los tres grandes, sin embargo, todavía es enorme. El título se antoja prácticamente imposible para los verdiblancos, cuya cuota alcanza los 100.0, frente al 1.44 del Barcelona, el 2.85 del Real Madrid y el 16.9 del Atlético. Los tres cumplieron esta semana con victorias ante Levante, Rayo y Real Sociedad. El Betis, en cualquier caso, puede empezar a mirar hacia arriba con argumentos cada vez más sólidos. Su gran arranque, unido a su capacidad para competir y ganar contra rivales directos y grandes de LaLiga, le ha colocado en una posición privilegiada. Tonybet ya le considera el principal candidato para hacerse con esa cuarta plaza que da acceso a la Champions. Los de Pellegrini sueñan en grande... y los números empiezan a dar motivos para hacerlo. La pelea por la permanencia presenta un escenario muy diferente. El Elche, con una cuota de 2.37, es ahora mismo el equipo que acompaña a los recién ascendidos Málaga (1.80) y Racing (2.75) entre los principales candidatos al descenso. El Valencia, actual colista después de un inicio de temporada especialmente complicado, todavía se mantiene fuera de ese grupo con una cuota de 4.33... aunque la cifra no deja de reducirse. articles.title: Hyrox cambia las reglas tras lo sucedido con la atleta que compitió cubierta en heces: "Cometimos un error"
articles.standfirst: Moritz Fuerste, cofundador alemán de Hyrox, anuncia el cambio inmediato del reglamento y pide disculpas por lo sucedido
articles.summary: Moritz Fuerste, cofundador alemán de Hyrox, anuncia el cambio inmediato del reglamento y pide disculpas por lo sucedido
articles.body: La compañía alemana Hyrox, organizadora de fitness en recintos cerrados, ha cambiado sus reglas después de que la campeona mundial Joanna Wietrzyk se hiciera sus necesidades durante una prueba celebrada el sábado en Pekín y siguiera compitiendo y acabara la prueba cubierta en heces. Moritz Fuerste, cofundador alemán de Hyrox, pidió disculpas "a todos los afectados directa o indirectamente por lo sucedido, así como con todos los que sintieron que no manejamos la situación como deberíamos haber hecho". Varios participantes en la prueba mostraron su sorpresa porque no se tomaran medidas. "La limpieza no se realizó en ese momento, sino al final del día, y hubo personas que se mancharon e incluso resbalaron por las heces", señaló una participante a EFE. "Hyrox cometió un error al no reaccionar inmediatamente durante la carrera. Al final es mi trabajo prever estos posibles incidentes y no lo hice. Por supuesto, comenzamos a mejorar los procesos del evento además de realizar cambios en el reglamento de inmediato", afirmó Fuerste en sus redes sociales. "A partir de este momento hay nuevas reglas y procedimientos en vigor para evitar que situaciones como esta vuelvan a ocurrir. Aprendemos y tratamos de mejorar cada día", añadió Fuerste. Hyrox ya había reaccionado al día siguiente de la prueba cuando anunció en un comunicado: "Reconocemos que esto puede, lógicamente, provocar frustración, preguntas y opiniones encendidas dentro de nuestra comunidad. Esas preocupaciones son legítimas y, como organizadores, debemos estar preparados para escucharlas, investigar lo ocurrido y responsabilizarnos para seguir mejorando".

articles.title: Nairobi beats London to host World Athletics Championships 2029 as Africa gets historic first
articles.summary: International Sports News: Nairobi has beaten London and Rome to win the right to host the World Athletics Championships 2029. The decision was confirmed at a World Athletics co.
articles.body: Nairobi has beaten London and Rome to win the right to host the World Athletics Championships 2029. The decision was confirmed at a World Athletics council meeting in Budapest. It will be the first time the global athletics championships are held in an African city.London had hoped to bring the event back to the city after successfully hosting the 2017 championships. Its bid was centred on the London Stadium, which also hosted athletics during the 2012 Olympic Games. However, Nairobi’s bid impressed the council and secured the historic opportunity for Kenya and the continent.Nairobi wins historic World Athletics Championships 2029 bidWorld Athletics president Sebastian Coe praised Nairobi’s proposal after the decision. He said the Kenyan capital presented “a compelling and emotional bid”.“We were fortunate to have four outstanding bids for 2029 and 2031, and this was not an easy decision for the council. With this decision today, we continue to fulfil our mission of growing athletics worldwide with the hosting of our World Athletics Championships in Asia, Africa and Europe over its next three editions. Nairobi presented a compelling and emotional bid, and taking the World Athletics Championships to Africa for the first time will be historic”, said Coe.The decision is a major moment for Kenya. The country has a long and successful history in middle- and long-distance running. Kenyan athletes have regularly challenged for medals at major global competitions.“It was important that the World Athletics Championships should come to Africa when we had the right host, the right bid and the right circumstances. Nairobi has demonstrated emphatically that this is their moment”, he added.Kenya finished second in the medal table at the 2025 World Athletics Championships. The team won seven gold medals and 11 medals overall.Nairobi had previously tried to host the 2025 championships. However, Tokyo was selected instead. The city has now secured another chance to stage the biggest event in international athletics.A major factor in the successful bid is the renovation of Kasarani Stadium. The venue is being upgraded ahead of the Africa Cup of Nations 2027. The improvements strengthened Nairobi’s case and provided confidence about its ability to host a major international sporting event.London’s bid was led by Athletic Ventures. articles.summary: Manchester United injury news ahead of Brighton as Carrick needs a responseManchester United have no time to sulk. The derby defeat to Manchester City was co...
articles.body:
Manchester United injury news ahead of Brighton as Carrick needs a response

Manchester United have no time to sulk. The derby defeat to Manchester City was contentious, the fallout has rumbled on, and the table already looks awkward. Four points from a possible 12 is a poor start by any standard, and Michael Carrick knows it.

He put it plainly enough. United have "got to get back to winning football matches". That is the job now, and the next chance comes in the Carabao Cup against Brighton at Old Trafford.

There is a revenge angle too. Brighton beat United in the FA Cup earlier in the year, and they remain a side capable of exposing any looseness in structure or intensity. United, for their part, are still waiting on several important players, and the availability list matters because this squad already looks stretched in key areas.

Here is the latest on the main Manchester United injury concerns before the Brighton clash, with the expected return dates based on the current information.

Luke Shaw close to return for Manchester United

Luke Shaw had started every Premier League game last season, so his absence in the derby stood out. The left-back picked up a knock in the 2-2 draw with Everton on September 6 and also missed the Champions League win over Sabah.

The good news is that the issue does not appear serious. Carrick made that clear when he said: "Close, very close, just not quite there. It's very small but unfortunately not for today."

That suggests Shaw is not far away, and United will hope he can return either for Brighton or the trip to Fulham . Given the lack of natural balance without him, his recovery matters. He gives United width, tempo in possession and a degree of calm that has been missing at times.

Potential return date: September 16 vs Brighton

Carlos Baleba set to wait longer after £70m move

Carlos Baleba arrived from Brighton for £70m, but he has yet to make his debut. United signed him carrying an ankle ligament injury suffered in pre-season against Strasbourg , and that has delayed his start at Old Trafford.

There was some optimism that he could be available before the international break, but that now looks unlikely. Facing his former club this week appears a stretch.

Carrick said: "He's got a little ankle issue. So, maybe a couple of weeks or so, maybe three weeks, we'll see. But we knew that before, so it's no major issue.

"It'll be great to have him back when we can. We're delighted with Carlos. I think huge potential, massive potential. I think it's a really exciting signing for us."

That is all encouraging in the medium term, but right now it is still theoretical. Baleba has talent, physicality and upside, but United need players on the pitch, not in the treatment room. A return after the international break looks the most realistic call.

Potential return date: October 10 vs Tottenham

Amad Diallo and Matthijs de Ligt latest updates

Amad Diallo was missing from the squad for the opening day defeat at newly promoted Hull after suffering an ankle problem in training. It came out of nowhere and has left United short of another attacking option during a period when sharpness in the final third has not been consistent.

There is still no firm timeframe from Carrick, which usually means caution. Early suggestions pointed to around six weeks out, and if that proves accurate then Amad is another one who is likely to return only after the international break.

That would put Tottenham at home in view, followed by a demanding run featuring Atletico Madrid , Leeds and Como away from home. United will need him fit soon enough, particularly if they want more penetration from wide areas.

Matthijs de Ligt is closer. The defender has been edging back after back surgery in May, and while there was concern when he missed a training session last week, it later emerged that he was simply on a designated rest day.

So there has been no setback, which is the key point. Carrick said: "We have to see. It's positive. He's trained really well but we're still managing it, when you're out for such a long period of time, you get to the final stages, pushing and pushing, and you've got to manage that last stage.

"It's important to get that balance right to take the next step.

"But he's on a good track, in a good place and it's great to have him back around us. Hopefully, some time soon."

That sounds like a player on the brink of availability. Whether he starts immediately is another matter, but United need depth and authority at centre-back, and De Ligt should provide both when fully ready.

Manuel Ugarte and Tom Heaton remain longer-term absentees

Manuel Ugarte has not played at all this season after suffering a ligament injury with Uruguay during the summer. It was a serious setback, and all indications are that United are taking a very long-term view on his rehabilitation.

The midfielder was stretchered off during Uruguay's 1-0 defeat by Spain in the group phase, and there is still no proper return window in place. The only clear progress so far is that he has been back working in the gym at Carrington with the medical and performance staff.

That is a start, nothing more. United will not see him any time soon, and the expectation remains that he will not return until 2027.

Tom Heaton is also still out. The veteran goalkeeper suffered a hamstring injury in pre-season against Paris Saint-Germain on August 8 and has not featured since. There have been very few updates, which leaves his situation vague.

As third-choice keeper, his absence does not alter the first-team picture dramatically, but United would still prefer to have experience available in reserve, especially with cup matches arriving early in the campaign.

The broader picture is straightforward. Shaw and De Ligt are close, Baleba and Amad are more likely to return after the international break, and Ugarte remains a long way off. For Carrick, that means no excuses and little room for drift. Brighton are next, and United need a reaction.

Further details around the latest Manchester United injury news will become clearer as the Brighton fixture approaches.

articles.title: Carlos decisive, Barella everywhere: the five best moments from Inter vs. Udinese
articles.summary: At the final whistle, San Siro erupts into song and applause for an Inter side who are brilliant, spectacular, entertaining and still winning. An early scare...
articles.body:
At the final whistle, San Siro erupts into song and applause for an Inter side who are brilliant, spectacular, entertaining and still winning. An early scare was needed to spark the flame, with two goals conceded in quick succession bringing out the Nerazzurri's attacking firepower. Matchday four brought a second consecutive comeback at home, once again from two goals down. This time, Chivu's side scored five, throwing themselves into the fightback and showing a ruthless desire to finish the job. The match against Udinese delivered another three points, taking Inter's tally to 12: four wins from four and a perfect record, something that had not happened since 2023/24. They share top spot with Roma, their next Serie A opponents. It was an open, thrilling contest, packed with moments of footballing brilliance that drew thunderous applause and technical gems that prompted gasps of admiration around the stands.

Let's relive Inter's clash with Udinese through five moments, five snapshots that have stayed in the memory from matchday four.

After 16 minutes, the scoreboard at San Siro reads Inter 0-2 Udinese. The Nerazzurri are stunned, caught cold by two incisive attacks from Runjaić's side. There is still everything to play for, but they need a spark to bring the game back to life, an opening blow to respond to the Bianconeri 's one-two punch. And it is quite literally a flash of brilliance that gets the contest back underway. In the 26th minute, Bastoni wins the ball back in midfield and Inter break forward. Mkhitaryan gets to the byline and sends a cross in from the left, but the Friulian defence clears. The ball falls to Carlos Augusto , who takes a touch and does not hesitate: the Brazilian unleashes a thunderous strike from more than 25 metres out. The ball flies beautifully through the air before finding the far corner to Okoye's left. A ferocious diagonal effort that brings the Nerazzurri and San Siro back to life, like a splash of cold water jolting everyone awake. It is Carlos' second goal in consecutive games, following his strike at the Bernabéu, and takes him level with his total number of goal involvements from the whole of last season. Carlos Augusto has made a flying start to the campaign, making his presence felt and proving decisive defensively too: he runs, wins the ball back, reads the game and keeps his concentration high. After Inter levelled through Barella , the Brazilian made another crucial intervention, stepping in ahead of Unai Gómez. Miller carries the ball into the final third and plays a one-two with Davis, receives the return pass and attempts to thread the ball through to Gómez. A brilliant idea, but Carlos reads it early, cuts out the passing lane and prevents the Spaniard from getting through on goal.

After Carlos Augusto's goal, the intensity of the Nerazzurri's pressure rises dramatically, and there is one player in particular who seems to be occupying three or four positions at once. Nicolò Barella is everywhere: snapping at opponents, disrupting passing lanes, making himself available and moving the ball on, showing the way. A technical and emotional leader. It is no coincidence that he is the one to score the deserved equaliser, with a goal that perfectly embodies his approach to the game: no ball is ever considered lost, even after hitting the deck. Barella is literally on the ground just moments before scoring the 2-2: the Nerazzurri number 23 slips inside the box after getting on the end of Thuram 's lay-off, but with all the electricity coursing through him, he somehow gets back to his feet in an instant and uses his momentum to dribble and shoot. He is in a tight position on the right, but Barella strikes the ball from high to low, giving it a swerve that completely wrong-foots Okoye. The goal, however, does not fully capture Barella's enormous contribution. He wins back the ball from which the move for the 2-2 begins, and he is the one who sends Diouf through, creating the opportunity for the 3-2. Nicolò roars, and the stadium roars with him. He beckons his teammates over with sweeping gestures before sprinting back towards the halfway line: a snapshot that encapsulates his powerful start to the season, a sign that the work has only just begun.

Marcus Thuram continues to make his mark, extending a run that stretches back to the end of last season, when the Tikus settled decisive matches for the Scudetto with a string of goals. After his header made it 2-2 against Napoli , Thuram scored the goal that sealed the comeback against Udinese, making it 3-2. After 57 minutes of physical battles and pressing, with chances thwarted by Okoye and the Bianconeri defence, Marcus was in the right place inside the box to turn home Diouf's third assist of the league campaign. Just like a week ago, his celebration is full of fury, reflecting his attitude on the pitch: aggression, leading the press as the first man to put pressure on the build-up, a desire to win the ball back and to drive his team forward. Thuram slides towards the stand, points to his chest and then puts his hands to his ears before finally breaking into his trademark smile. A smile that has been a constant for months in the Nerazzurri shirt, with Marcus having contributed to 12 goals in the league since April (eight goals and four assists). Only Malen , with 15 goal involvements, has done better in Serie A over the same period. It was a complete performance against Udinese, earning him the Man of the Match award at the final whistle. Powerful, inspirational, decisive: keep it going, Marcus!

"Some players would have taken the shot from there, but I saw that Pio had found some space and I thought I'd play him in." Piotr Zielinski 's words, as he reflected after the match on the visionary assist that put Pio Esposito through for the 4-2. A moment of brilliance conceived and executed in an instant, completely taking the Udinese defence out of the equation. A gem to cap a wonderful team move built on quality, quick combinations, understanding and technique. Quality was precisely the aspect Piotr highlighted when discussing Inter's comeback, and it flowed beautifully from his feet. Another masterclass in midfield, with an outstanding display in terms of the quality of his play, his timing and his distribution, crowned by that sumptuous assist that allowed Pio to score the fourth goal and put Inter firmly in control of the match. A perfectly weighted ball played through the middle, spotting a narrow channel and threading the pass through it to catch the Bianconeri defenders off guard, as they prepared to throw themselves in front of any potential effort from the Pole. Instead, the result was to put Esposito one-on-one with the goalkeeper and send San Siro into celebration for the fourth time.

When Bonny puts the ball into the net in the 79th minute to make it 5-2, Thuram springs from the bench to join him by the corner flag and celebrate. It was a goal Ange-Yoan wanted and fought for, throwing himself into a slide to turn Okoye's save from his first effort into a goal at the second attempt. It was another reminder that those who come on during the game are ready to give 100 per cent and make their contribution. The team's embrace showed how everyone was involved, while the level of concentration maintained on the pitch demonstrated their determination to make their mark. Chivu reiterated the importance of this aspect after the match during a long and demanding season in which Inter want to be protagonists. Players called upon from the bench can make an impact and prove decisive: against Udinese, Bonny did exactly that, while Stankovic came close too, clipping the post with a free-kick in the closing stages. Inter remain perfect after four matches, driven by a strong and united group capable of responding to setbacks while always maintaining their identity.

Barnsley have signed defender Jubril Okedina on a one-year deal with the option of a further year.

The 25-year-old Malawi international came through Tottenham Hotspur's youth setup and later joined Cambridge United, where he made 138 appearances in all competitions.

articles.summary: The Penguins have made their first significant executive hire since the Hoffman Family’s acquisition of the team was approved in June. The franchise announce...
articles.body:
The Penguins have made their first significant executive hire since the Hoffman Family's acquisition of the team was approved in June.

The franchise announced Monday that Marcel Braithwaite has been named the Penguins' new president of business operations.

Braithwaite most recently served as SVP of business operations for the Houston Astros. The Astros credit him with overseeing multiple renovations of the club's ballpark while also leading the development of a spring training complex in Florida during his 14 years with the franchise.

He will now take that experience into guiding upcoming improvements to PPG Paints Arena, per Eddie Maisonet of Chron.com.

The arena last underwent major renovations ahead of the 2023-24 season. The transfer of its lease to the Hoffman Family was approved in March.

Braithwaite said he wanted PPG Paints to be a "a year-round crown jewel for the citizens of Pittsburgh," per Maisonet.

"They've got a ton of experience and certainly the motivation behind them, which I think is going to be really beneficial to the city of Pittsburgh from a tax base increase from a resurgence of downtown and the opportunity to bring more fans to come to the games and the other events that we host at PPG," Braithwaite said, per Maisonet.

The Hoffman family first talked about their intention to bring in a new president of business operations during their introductory press conference in June. New governor Geoff Hoffman said at the time his family wanted to be "present" but not "micromanage the team."

The role was previously held on an interim basis by Teddy Werner, who the franchise said last December would serve in that position until the sale of the team from the Fenway Sports Group had closed at a $1.7 billion valuation.

The Penguins are preparing to open training camp Thursday before kicking off the preseason next Monday, Sept. 21 against the visiting Buffalo Sabres .

articles.title: ‘Some Positive Things’ — Mike Vrabel Reveals Patriots Rookies Who Impressed Him in Week 1
articles.summary: The New England Patriots may have opened the season with a loss; however, the head coach, Mike Vrabel, still found a few things worth taking from the perform...
articles.body:
The New England Patriots may have opened the season with a loss; however, the head coach, Mike Vrabe l, still found a few things worth taking from the performances of his rookie class. Three first-year players in particular caught his attention after New England 's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks .

Tight end Eli Raridon , edge rusher Gabe Jacas, and linebacker Namdi Obiazor all made their NFL debuts against the Seahawks. None had much of a statistical line to point to outside of Jacas' sack and Raridon's touchdown; however, Vrabel was more interested in the way they handled their first real test.

Mike Vrabel Points to Eli Raridon, Gabe Jacas and Namdi Obiazor

Vrabel discussed the three rookies during his Monday appearance on The Greg Hill Show and made it clear that he was not judging their first games strictly by the box score.

"I felt like some of our young players did some decent things. I know it's not gonna show up in the stats, but I thought Eli [Raridon] tried to block and tried to battle. He had a few instinctive plays where he was responsible for somebody, and they ran out of there, and he kind of found the next guy who would be coming down into that position. There were some things that I thought were instinctive. I thought Gabe [Jacas] had his best showing. I thought [Namdi Obiazor] played good on special teams… To be able to get some of those younger players who have never played, and that's their first game, those are some positive things. I don't think people realize what that environment is like."

Raridon had the biggest moment of the three. The third-round pick out of Notre Dame caught a two-yard touchdown from Drake Maye for the first points of the Patriots' season. He finished with one reception, except his role went beyond that catch.

Raridon played 38 offensive snaps, or 54% of the Patriots' offensive total, as the second TE behind Hunter Henry . The head coach specifically pointed to his blocking and his ability to react when a play did not unfold exactly as expected. Those details won't do much for a fantasy score, but they mattered to the Patriots' coaching staff in a player's first NFL game.

Jacas had a more obvious statistical impact. The second-round pick, selected 55th overall after the Patriots traded up with the Los Angeles Chargers , recorded his first career sack against the Seahawks. He fought through a double team, stayed with the play, and brought down Drew Lock.

That was notable because Jacas had a relatively quiet preseason after missing much of the spring. Vrabel had already talked about wanting more from him, and his debut gave the coaching staff something concrete to build on.

The three rookies were part of a larger first-year group that saw the field in Seattle. Caleb Lomu, Tanner Arkin, Dametrious Crownover, Quintayvious Hutchins, and Channing Canada also suited up, while Karon Prunty, Erick Hunter, and Behren Morton were inactive.

For now, Vrabel's attention appears to be on the players who gave the Patriots something in their first taste of regular-season football.

In a matter of weeks after Ilja Dragunov left WWE, the former NXT and NXT UK Champion has found a new home in Tony Khan's AEW .

Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp (via Sports Illustrated) reports that Dragunov is expected to sign a free agent deal with AEW. He would not be the only WWE-released star to jump ship, joining the New Level (formerly the New Day) and the Motor City Machine Guns.

After losing the NXT Championship to Williams, Dragunov made his main roster debut on the Monday Night RAW after WrestleMania 40 in April 2024. During his main roster career, he would win the United States Championship once, beating Sami Zayn, before losing it to Hayes a couple of months later.

articles.title: Why Patrick Mahomes' impotent passing stats in win over Broncos were great news for Chiefs
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes looked healthy in his return from his 2025 season-ending knee injury in the Chiefs' Monday night home opener of 2026, but there also should b...
articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes returned from the first major injury of his career — a torn ACL and LCL in his left knee — to lead the Chiefs to a huge Monday night 2026 NFL season-opening win over the Broncos . Although Mahomes turned in one of his least-prolific passing performances against Denver 's defense, it didn't take long for Kansas City to know its franchise quarterback is back to his old self.

The Chiefs missed the playoffs for the first time with Mahomes as the starting QB in 2025. He went 6-8 and then the team lost all three games he missed late to finish 6-11. Now the Chiefs are 1-0, with a win over the 0-1 Broncos , who went 14-3 to dethrone the Chiefs as AFC West champions last season.

The 31-10 dominant home victory by Kansas City was stamped by the running of new feature back Kenneth Walker III. The Seahawks ' Super Bowl 60 MVP pounded the Broncos for 173 rushing yards , including a 60-yard TD. The defense took care of the rest with four sacks and two takeaways from Broncos QB Bo Nix , on a windy night not making for prime passing conditions.

Mahomes did provide the big early highlight, a dazzling 15-yard scoring run up the middle to match his jersey number and indicate his clean bill of heath. But when looking at his passing stats (15-of-27, 184 yards, 2 TDs, INT, 6.8 yards per attempt, 86.0 passer rating), there might be concern for continued issues with the receiving corps.

As Walker stole the show with 169 scrimmage yards and 2 total TDs in his debut, the Chiefs also trumpeted their less Mahomes-dependent offensive philosophy for '26. Andy Reid and offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy have reunited this season with the smart plan of taking pressure off Mahomes.

The Chiefs ran 38 times in total for 220 yards in relation to 29 Mahomes dropbacks. That 57-43 run-pass ratio isn't often seen in Kansas City under Reid.

It's also rare for Mahomes to throw for 185 or fewer yards. In 12 such regular-season games with Mahomes, the Chiefs are 10-2. In the playoffs, the Chiefs are 7-0 when Mahomes throws for 255 or fewer yards.

There will be some natural big passing games ahead for Mahomes, maybe as early as Week 2 at home next Sunday night, when the reeling Colts defense — which just gave up 506 total yards and 41 points to the Ravens at home — comes to Kansas City.

Then again, the Ravens ran all over the Colts with their own power back, Derrick Henry , and their defense wasn't challenged much. The Chiefs acquired Walker for his early-down home-run ability and strong red zone finishing, or their long missing workhorse in the mold of Henry.

When Mahomes wasn't making much noise with the downfield passing game in the past, the Chiefs didn't have the potential to pivot to a run-heavy attack to take advantage of soft zone defenses still worried about Mahomes' dangerous deep throwing. That's why they had to splurge on Walker in free agency for how he carried the Seahawks' balanced offense.

The Chiefs were the Super Bowl champions other teams were trying to emulate, so go figure they would do some copycatting of them own. Reid has tended to get too pass-happy at times, going back to his days in Philadelphia .

The revamped active defense remains a strength and needed this brand of physical ball-control offense to match the new winning identity. As the running game continues to deliver, it also will lead to Mahomes shredding defenses with shots off play-action again soon.

Mahomes getting back in MVP passing form is rather scary. Mahomes as a clutch complement to the running game and defense? That's downright frightening.

articles.title: Coach of Hyrox World Champion Who Soiled Herself During Competition Speaks Out, Slams ‘Personal Attacks’ Against Athlete
articles.summary: Joanna Wietrzyk, 22, divided opinion for continuing a race in Beijing on Saturday, Sept. 12, after she became ill
articles.body:
The coach of a Hyrox athlete who faced backlash for soiling herself during a race has spoken out in her defense

Joanna Wietrzyk, 22, divided opinion for continuing a race in Beijing on Saturday, Sept. 12, after she became ill

Coach Chris Bayers called the situation unforeseen and emphasized the need for fair judgment in a statement he shared on Instagram in the wake of the controversy

The coach of a Hyrox athlete who divided opinion after soiling herself during a race has spoken out in her defense.

Joanna Wietrzyk, 22, was criticized after she continued to compete in the Hyrox race for ages 16-24 at the National Speed Skating Oval in Beijing on Saturday, Sept. 12, after becoming ill.

Photos and videos circulating online appeared to show fecal matter on her legs, and the Australian athlete posted a now-deleted selfie of herself from what seemed to be a hospital bed on Instagram after winning the race in 1 hour, 1 minute, 23 seconds.

"Go hard or go home … a win is a win. In all seriousness, thank you for all the support. I'll be back soon x," she wrote, per The Athletic and news.com.au , while commenters online have argued that she posed health risks by staying in the race.

In response to the backlash, Wietrzyk's coach, Chris Bayens, defended her in a statement that he posted on Instagram.

"What happened was an extraordinary set of circumstances that were unforeseen, rapidly evolving and almost impossible to fully comprehend in real time," he said.

"Decisions were made under competition conditions by an athlete, judges and officials, all responding to a situation none of them could reasonably have prepared for," Bayens continued.

Bayens said it would be easy to "construct the perfect response" in hindsight, and explained that "lessons can be taken" from the decisions made at the time.

"But judging someone's intent, character or morality through the clarity of hindsight is neither fair nor honest," he added. "Sport occasionally produces moments that are imperfect and deeply human."

"Discussion is legitimate. The hatred and personal attacks that have followed are not," Bayens insisted.

Bayens captioned the post, "The physical health and performance of an athlete is my job."

"The mental health of athletes is shaped far more by the community around them, and right now that community should take a hard look at itself," he added.

Bayens said, "No one is perfect, not in sport, not on social media, not in real life. What happened was extraordinary. The hatred that has followed is ugly."

PEOPLE has reached out to Chris Bayens for further comment, but did not immediately hear back.

Hyrox bosses have also responded to the incident, with co-founder Moritz Fürste apologizing to "all that were directly or indirectly affected," as well as pledging changes, in a statement posted to Instagram on Monday, Sept. 14.

"Hyrox made a mistake by not reacting immediately during the race," he wrote. "In the end it is my job to foresee these potential incidents — and I did not."

He continued, "Of course, we started improving event processes, plus making rule book changes immediately. As of this moment, there are new rules and procedures in place to prevent situations like this from happening again."

Hyrox, founded in Germany in 2017, is described on its website as "the fastest-growing fitness sport in the world."

Participants run around 0.6 miles and visit a functional workout station, repeating the process eight times. Functional workouts include sled pushes, rowing, burpee broad jumps and wall balls.

Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE's free sports newsletter — sign up now!

In a previous Instagram statement addressing the incident, Hyrox organizers wrote, "In this instance, an unforeseen situation arose in which protocols designed for elite competition and mass participation became blurred, creating ambiguity in how they were applied and understood."

"We will continue to listen. We will continue to learn. And, above all, we will continue to put the welfare and dignity of the athletes at the center of what comes next," they added.

Hello everyone, and welcome to the live blog for the Zimbabwe vs Australia 1st ODI in Harare.

Australia recovered from a 107/4 wobble to post 294/8, with Matt Renshaw's maiden ODI century (109 off 94) providing the foundation for the late innings.

Oliver Peake provided valuable support, making 30 off 40, as he and Renshaw put together a 50-run partnership to rebuild the innings.

Zimbabwe's Newman Nyamhuri was the star with the ball, claiming his maiden five-wicket haul. He also removed Peake and Renshaw late, finishing with 5 wickets.

Australia's finishing was underwhelming. They managed only 66 runs in the final 10 overs, with just one boundary in the last seven overs, leaving them short of what looked like a potentially bigger total but Blessing Muzarabani's final two overs restricted Australia effectively.

However, Sikandar Raza had an expensive day, while his 43rd over included a no-ball for having too few fielders inside the circle.

Brad Evans returned to break the 72-run 5th-wicket partnership immediately after the 31st over, as he dismissed Alex Carey for 27. Matt Renshaw took full control following Carey's departure. He reached a well-constructed half-century off 55 deliveries before shifting gears.

Oliver Peake showed great composure and rotated strike to keep the scoreboard ticking. Zimbabwe tightened things up through Raza to concede only 3 runs off the 40th over. Australia entered the final Powerplay firmly placed at 228/5 with Renshaw well-set on 75*.

Alex Carey and Matt Renshaw went through the gears methodically to halt Zimbabwe's momentum after they walked in together following Connolly's wicket in the 18th over.

Raza rotated his spin options alongside Brian Bennett and Wellington Masakadza to apply pressure, but the Australian pair showed clean judgment and kept the scoreboard ticking. The pair have 51 runs without losing a wicket in this 10-over block.

This has helped Australia consolidate their innings to 167/4, setting the stage for an aggressive finish heading into the final 20 overs.

Newman Nyamhuri carried his powerplay momentum into the middle overs, having Josh Inglis edge behind to Brendan Taylor for just 4, which reduced Australia to 83/3 in the 13th over.

Cooper Connolly shifted gears to anchor the innings, and launched three clean sixes to reach his half-century off just 44 deliveries to push Australia past the 100-run mark. Just as Connolly looked primed to dominate the middle overs, veteran Sikandar Raza dismissed him for 51 by going through his defence.

Brad Evans struck early in the 2nd over, cleaning up Travis Head for just 4 to put Australia on the back foot at 10/1. However, Mitchell Marsh played fearless cricket and put up a 50-run second-wicket stand. He tore into the bowling with a brisk 36 off 28 deliveries (6 fours, 1 six), punishing anything loose from Evans and Muzarabani.

In the 10th over, Newman Nyamhuri produced a vital breakthrough on the final ball of his first over, having Marsh caught by Bennett for 36. At the other end, Connolly has held firm with a steady 19*, joined by new batter Josh Inglis as Zimbabwe's late powerplay scalp keeps honours even after the first 10 overs.

Australia won the toss and opted to bat first.

Australia are back in Zimbabwe for the first time in over a decade. The first of three ODIs gets underway at Harare Sports Club on Tuesday, September 15, with both nations using this assignment to sharpen their preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup, a tournament Zimbabwe will co-host alongside South Africa and Namibia.

Sikandar Raza leads Zimbabwe into this series off the back of a 2-1 ODI series win over Bangladesh, which gives the hosts a foundation of recent confidence to build on.

Australia make the trip without their captain Pat Cummins and frontline pacer Mitchell Starc, but hardly a squad stripped of quality. Josh Hazlewood provides the pace threat, Mitchell Marsh adds batting firepower and all-round value, and Travis Head brings proven big-match experience.

The numbers strongly favour the visitors. Australia have won eight of the nine ODIs played between these two nations, and nothing about Zimbabwe's recent form suggests a shift in that dynamic is coming. Still, a World Cup co-host playing at home, motivated and fresh off a series win, will make Australia earn everything they get.

articles.title: Calhanoglu at risk of missing Roma clash after being ruled out of Inter 5-3 Udinese
articles.summary: Hakan Calhanoglu was not named in Cristian Chivu’s matchday squad for Inter’s 5-3 comeback victory over Udinese on Monday evening, and reports on Tuesday ind...
articles.body:
Hakan Calhanoglu was not named in Cristian Chivu's matchday squad for Inter 's 5-3 comeback victory over Udinese on Monday evening, and reports on Tuesday indicate that he is at a high risk of missing the top-of-the-table clash against Roma this coming weekend as well.

Calhanoglu a strong doubt for Roma vs. Inter

Goals from Carlos Augusto , Nicolo Barella , Marcus Thuram , Pio Esposito and Ange-Yoan Bonny gave Inter a 5-3 victory over Udinese in San Siro on Monday evening, despite the fact that the Nerazzurri had trailed 2-0 after the first 16 minutes.

MILAN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 14: Ange-Yoan Bonny of FC Internazionale Milano celebrates scoring his team's fifth goal with teammates Curtis Jones, Marcus Thuram and Francesco Pio Esposito during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Udinese Calcio at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on September 14, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images)

Chivu went with a midfield three of Barella, Piotr Zielinski and Henrikh Mkhitaryan on the night, introducing Curtis Jones and Aleksandar Stankovic from the subs bench in the second half.

Calhanoglu was not named in the matchday squad due to adductor fatigue.

According to the latest updates from La Gazzetta dello Sport on Tuesday morning, Calhanoglu will have further assessments carried out this afternoon, but as things stand, there is a large chance that he is not able to play against Roma this Saturday either.

MILAN, ITALY – MAY 17: Hakan Calhanoglu of FC Internazionale Milano poses for a photo with the Coppa Campioni d'Italia and Coppa Italia trophies following the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Hellas Verona FC at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on May 17, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Inter also lost England international John Stones to injury midway through the Udinese clash on Monday night and he is also expected to miss out on the Roma clash this weekend. He is likely to return after the international break.

Saturday's game against Roma is a key clash in the race for the 2026-27 Serie A title given that the Nerazzurri and Giallorossi are the only two sides in the division with their 100% win records still intact. That will come to an end at the Stadio Olimpico at 17.00 BST on Saturday evening.

articles.title: Jürgen Klopp plans on naming two blocks of players in September
articles.summary: The legendary coach has an interesting idea…
articles.body:
Jürgen Klopp joining the DFB has followed a similar path as many recent Germany managers. An established German coach with success in the Bundesliga, and seen as someone who could be a savior to the German national team after Joachim Löw. Unfortunately, that wasn't meant to be for Hansi Flick or Julian Nagelsmann. Now with Klopp, Germany can turn a new page, and it appears that it will be an interesting chapter.

An interesting story in the Klopp era was that the former Liverpool boss had big plans for change at the DFB and based on reports from this week, that is an understatement. According to reports from Sky Germany report Florian Plettenberg , Jürgen Klopp is planning to name an XXL squad on Thursday for the start of the UEFA Nations League campaign.

Reports state that the new manager wants to see as many players as possible with no exact number of players has decided yet. There are set to be two blocks of players for the four matches. It is certainly interesting verbiage to use here. Will there be 15 or so players that are staples with two separate blocks of additional players that will split the halves of the international break?

It is very unclear on what this all means but it will be interesting to see what happens. It is certainly an opportunity to really experiment but it almost seems like there is no clear plan yet. Luckily, Klopp's leash will be a long one but this seems fairly unconventional. Let him cook?

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Shooting an Imaginary Ball Goes Viral Amid Team USA Ball-Distribution Controversy
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark spent the 2026 FIBA Women’s World Cup in Germany winning gold with Team USA, but the tournament was not without its drama. Clips circulated dur...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark spent the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup in Germany winning gold with Team USA, but the tournament was not without its drama.

Clips circulated during the group stage showing teammates seemingly avoiding passing to Clark, and fans spent weeks debating how involved she actually was in the offense. One moment in particular cut through all the noise, and it was a funny one.

Caitlin Clark's imaginary shot draws attention from Team USA fans

A clip showed Clark copying her shooting motion on the sideline during a Team USA setting. The moment looked like a playful response to not receiving the ball during the sequence.

"Caitlin Clark NEVER got the ball on Team USA so she had to shoot an imaginary one," BrickCenter wrote with the video.

The video took off quickly, partly because the ball-distribution debate had already been brewing for days. Clips from the 105-64 win over Czech Republic had gone viral earlier in the week showing Breanna Stewart , Paige Bueckers , and Rhyne Howard passing up open looks to Clark on multiple possessions. Clark herself stayed diplomatic about it, saying it was hard to decide who to pass to when everyone around her was so talented.

The clip did not prove that Clark was upset. It showed a player keeping her shooting rhythm during a break in the action. That small detail helped the video travel across social media.

Team USA wins gold with Caitlin Clark despite the noise

Clark ended the tournament on a high note. In the gold medal game against France, she came off the bench, played 13 minutes, and scored 12 points on 4-of-5 shooting to go with three assists. Team USA won 97-79 after trailing France by 14 points early, and Clark finished as the team leader in total assists with 32 across the tournament.

Then came the locker room celebration, which produced its own viral moment. Clark was caught on camera spraying champagne directly into her own eye, which BrickCenter also shared and which rounded out a tournament full of sideline clips that kept her in the social media conversation from start to finish.

articles.title: Boston Celtics’ Neemias Queta Opens Up on Fighting for Minutes With Mitchell Robinson
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics added Mitchell Robinson to their ranks to beef up their frontcourt depth this offseason, and Neemias Queta recently weighed in on how he’l...
articles.body:
The Boston Celtics added Mitchell Robinson to their ranks to beef up their frontcourt depth this offseason, and Neemias Queta recently weighed in on how he'll mesh with the former No. 36 pick this upcoming season.

After establishing himself as the Boston Celtics ' starting center this past season, Queta signed a four-year, $56 million contract extension. But with Robinson's arrival, it remains to be seen how he'll keep his starting job and minutes.

"I'm not too worried about that. That's a Joe (Mazzulla) to figure out," Queta told Celtics on CLNS. "I'm out there just welcoming my new teammate with open arms. Mitchell's going to be a great addition for us. I'm extremely happy I don't have to go against him anymore because he used to get all these rebounds."

"It's going to be good to have him on our side, being able to have a player that's so accomplished — being able to guard multiple positions. One of the best rebounders the league has ever seen. So, nothing but welcome with open arms for him. And I'm excited to be his teammate," he added.

Boston Celtics News: Neemias Queta shares what he has been up to this offseason

In the same interview, Neemias Queta said he has spent the summer sharpening his game on both ends of the floor, which has been evident while playing for Portugal in the FIBA World Cup qualifiers .

"I've been working on different facets of the game, being more versatile. Offensively, being more complete, whether it's making quick decisions with the ball or there's a pass, being able to go and get my own shot, and defensively; being able to be in the right spots earlier," Queta said.

"And communicate a little bit more. The same old stuff; the space on the floor, as well. Being able to shoot. It's just been a good offseason to work, and I've been working on pretty much everything," he added.

The 27-year-old center is coming off a career year in 2025-26, averaging 10.2 points, 8.4 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.3 blocks on 65.3 percent shooting from the field across 76 regular-season appearances for the Boston Celtics.

articles.title: Lavezzi opens up on post-retirement depression and Messi support
articles.summary: Former Argentina forward Ezequiel Lavezzi has opened up on how close friend Lionel Messi helped him through depression and the "void" of life after retiremen...
articles.body:
Former Argentina forward Ezequiel Lavezzi has opened up on how close friend Lionel Messi helped him through depression and the "void" of life after retirement.

Lavezzi enjoyed successful spells at Napoli and Paris Saint-Germain as well as helping Argentina reach the 2014 World Cup final, where they were beaten 1-0 by Germany after extra time.

The 41-year-old finished his playing career in November 2019 after a spell at Hebei China Fortune.

Lavezzi revealed in an interview with Amazon Prime Italia how he had struggled to adapt after hanging up his boots, but also focused on the close bonds with former team-mates which helped him through tough times and on towards recovery.

"When I stopped playing, there was a void, and there was nothing to fill it," Lavezzi said.

"I struggled with depression, I was hospitalised. I am taking medication and undergoing treatment, and I am slowly recovering.

"The arrival of my son changed my life, he brings me so much joy and makes me feel alive. He gave me the strength to keep going."

Lavezzi added: "To those who suffer, I say that with humility and desire, you can overcome it. The world of football has been very close to me, so many have been close to me, like Messi, (Sergio) Aguero , Paolo Cannavaro .

"I have a special friendship with Messi, we talk about many things, he is a fantastic person."

articles.title: Ian Wright reveals incredible Mark Viduka Celtic dressing-room walkout in Inverness disaster
articles.summary: Ian Wright has recalled the remarkable moment Mark Viduka refused to return for the second half of Celtic’s infamous Scottish Cup defeat to Inverness Caledon...
articles.body:
Ian Wright has recalled the remarkable moment Mark Viduka refused to return for the second half of Celtic's infamous Scottish Cup defeat to Inverness Caledonian Thistle.

The 3-1 loss at Celtic Park in February 2000 ultimately cost John Barnes his job, but Wright has revealed the turmoil had already begun inside the dressing room at half-time.

Speaking on The Green Room, the former Celtic striker recalled Viduka beginning to remove his kit as Barnes and assistant Eric Black questioned what he was doing.

Wright said via The Overlap: "Yeah, Inverness Caledonian Thistle. He [Viduka] just started taking his gear off. I've never seen it before.

"You know, we're losing obviously Caledonian Thistle and came halftime the fans are booing, going crazy.

"He just came in and you know when someone just like the end of the game you start taking your gear off. Started taking his gear off and Barnes and Eric Black said what you doing?

"He says, 'F*** this man. I've had enough of this.'"

Wright claims Viduka then headed for the shower, leaving Barnes needing to make an unexpected half-time substitution.

Wright continued: "When they were talking to him and he just went into the shower and then Barnes went, 'Wright', I go for f*** sake, 'Wright get stripped, he's not coming back, you're a disgrace.'

"But it was like one of those when you're watching it in real time, it's like a film. You can't believe what you're seeing."

Viduka's absence was attributed to a knee injury by his agent at the time, while reports also suggested there had been a dressing-room confrontation involving the Australian and Black.

Roy Keane, who was listening to Wright recount the incident, admitted he could understand a player reaching breaking point mentally, although he stressed Viduka's actions were wrong.

Keane said: "That's not right but also when a player's mindset when your head goes…"

Keane replied: "No, I get that, of course I'm saying it's not right. But also, a player, when your head's gone, the head's gone, isn't it?"

Wright then said: "He went to the point of no return."

Celtic were actually trailing 2-1 at the interval rather than 1-0, with Wright replacing Viduka for the second half.

There was to be no comeback as Inverness completed a stunning 3-1 victory at Parkhead. Barnes was dismissed just two days later, bringing his ill-fated spell as Celtic manager to an end.

articles.title: Southend boss Dyer pledges to keep attacking style
articles.summary: Southend United boss Kieron Dyer urges fans not to get too giddy yet, but says they will maintain their attacking style.
articles.body:
Southend United boss Kieron Dyer says fans cannot get too giddy with their fine start but has promised to keep playing attacking football.

The Shrimpers go into Tuesday's National League game at home to Tamworth fifth in the table, three points behind early leaders Boreham Wood.

Southend have won four of their opening seven league matches under new boss Dyer who is in his first managerial role following a glittering career at Ipswich Town, Newcastle United and with England.

"In the worst possible way, winning three games to start off was a bad kind of thing because everybody gets a bit giddy and 'we're going to win the league'," the 47-year-old told BBC Radio Essex.

"I want everyone to think we have a great chance to win the league, but you've got to remember we are a really new team, with new coaching staff and new ways of playing.

"We've got to be really happy with our players and how quickly they've adjusted and got points on the board."

Dyer is already bringing his attacking playing style to the way he is setting up the Shrimpers, who lost in the play-offs in 2025-2026.

They've scored 14 goals in seven matches, taking six points from a possible nine at Roots Hall.

"We have to make this place a fortress. We had the set-back against Kidderminster , but our three performances at home have been of a good, high quality - with control and exciting football.

"Again, I want us to be really positive. I'm going to put as many flair players on the pitch as possible and feed them and let them cause havoc. So buckle in, and hopefully we give the fans something to sing about."

Tamworth have won just one of their opening seven games, and are 22nd in the table, conceding 19 goals so far.

"They're very good at what they do. They play two up. They try to bring chaos to a game, and they want it to be transitional" Dyer added.

"That's why they've scored a lot of goals (13), but I think it's also why they've conceded a lot of goals, too (19). We feel we can really expose their weaknesses.

"We'll make a few changes and try to get some real freshness. They pose a threat, but if we do what we want to do I think this game should be ok for us."

articles.title: Kentucky Wildcats crack top ten for elite Class of 2027 forward
articles.summary: AJ Williams is down to ten schools, and the Kentucky Wildcats, among with many other top programs, are among those listed.
articles.body:
AJ Williams is down to ten, and Mark Pope's Kentucky Wildcats are among those listed.

Pope hasn't had the best luck recruiting since making the jump to Kentucky, but things are starting to change. The addition of Class of 2027 forward Ryan Hampton marked a huge win for Pope and his staff, and there have been plenty of other elite recruits that are still including Kentucky as they start to narrow their options down.

Williams was one of the latest to drop an updated list of where he's going to play next season, and listed as the top player from Georgia and the second-best small forward, every program in the nation would love to attract the 6-foot-7 star. Here's the list: BYU, Georgia, Mississippi State, Illinois, Duke, Auburn, Kentucky, North Carolina, Arkansas, and Georgia Tech. It's an interesting list, one that doesn't include other blue-blood programs like Michigan State or Kansas.

Williams is going to finish up his high school career at Eagle's Landing Christian Academy. He's been ranked as the fifth-best player in the nation, per 247Sports, and was the top player in the Class of 2028 before reclassifying. There's good reason to believe that the 17-year-old forward could be the best player in the class as well. He dominated the Nike EYBL 17U circuit.

"Williams, 17, played on the Nike EYBL 17U circuit this summer with Team CP3 and established himself as one of the league's most productive scorers. He averaged 20.9 points, 8.1 rebounds and 1.4 assists while shooting 41.8 percent from the field and 31.1 percent from 3-point range," Tobias Bass and Brendan Marks of the New York Times wrote.

The excitement around the star forward is real, and hopefully he'll be able to bring that to Kentucky next season.

articles.title: Nottingham Forest fans' plea over stadium expansion
articles.summary: A fan group says the proposed City Ground development is a "historic opportunity for our region".
articles.body:
A Nottingham Forest supporters' group has written an open letter asking councillors to back expansion plans for its stadium, saying "it is the City Ground's time".

Rushcliffe Borough Council's planning committee will meet on Wednesday to consider applications from the club on proposed changes to the ground.

In June last year, the committee granted full planning permission to increase its overall capacity to 35,000, followed in January by the club submitting another set of applications to take the capacity to more than 50,000.

The Nottingham Forest Supporters' Trust (NFST) urged the authority not to let concerns over transport and supporter movement on matchdays further delay the project.

The applications consist of a bid for full planning permission to redevelop the Peter Taylor Stand and Trent End, as well as for "demolition of existing buildings/structures", and outline planning permission to redevelop the Brian Clough Stand.

Rushcliffe's planning officers have recommended councillors on the committee approve the applications, subject to conditions.

It comes days after MPs in Nottingham issued a joint statement backing development of the stadium.

The trust's letter to the committee calls Wednesday's vote a "historic opportunity for our region", adding the message was "clear and overwhelming" from fans in their support of the proposals.

Asif Naidu, NFST chair, said: "Wednesday is a historic opportunity to secure the future of our historic home. We simply have to grasp it.

"The case for approval is incredibly strong. It has clear and widespread support across the region, the club has outgrown the current ground and it is a golden and rare investment opportunity.

"Any concerns over transport and supporter flow, while understandable, can be resolved and are manageable, so they shouldn't be a barrier to giving the project the go-ahead.

"It is the City Ground's time. Let's make history on Wednesday."
